chunks: And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from Dāwūd ibn al-Nuʿmān, from Abū Ayyūb, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I heard Abū ʿAbdِ اللَّهِ عليه السلام say: “If a boy is approached by death and he makes a bequest before reaching maturity, his bequest is valid for blood relatives, and it is not valid for strangers.”

key_terms.الْغُلَامَ: a boy who has not yet reached legal maturity
key_terms.الْمَوْتُ: death, here referring to the approach of death
key_terms.لَمْ يُدْرِكْ: he had not yet reached maturity

ai.seo_question: Is the will of a minor valid in Islam if he has not yet reached maturity?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling about the bequest of a boy who has not yet reached maturity when death comes upon him. It states that such a bequest is accepted when directed to kin, but it is not accepted when made for non-relatives.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5453 - Ali ibn Al-Hakam narrated from Dawud ibn Al-Nuʿman from Abu Ayyub from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (as) say:
"If a boy is on his deathbed and makes a will before reaching maturity, his will is valid if it is for his close relatives, but it is not valid for strangers."
